findings.reason: the plan's §1 motivation and its constant's justification are both wrong for altair; the honest change names the existing row-limit mechanism (disable it, or bind `trace_max_points` to it in the plan text and docstring) rather than silently sitting under a limit the plan never mentions.
findings.text: the plan's altair premise is inverted and its new constant is coupled to an unmentioned existing mechanism: `_render_timeseries_alt` builds `df` from every sample (alt.py:377) into `alt.Chart(df)` (alt.py:386, alt.py:404), but altair's default data transformer raises `MaxRowsError` above 5000 rows — verified in the repo venv (altair 6.1.0) that `alt.Chart(DataFrame of 300000 rows).mark_line().encode(...).to_dict()` raises `MaxRowsError: The number of rows in your dataset (300000) is greater than the maximum allowed (5000)`; imas-ink never calls `alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()` (no `max_rows`/`data_transformers` reference anywhere in `imas_ink/`), so today the altair trace renderer does not write a 1.7–3.4 MB chart, it errors at render; the plan then fixes it by picking `trace_max_points = 4000` — just under altair's 5000 throw — while presenting that constant as freely settable style, so a user override above 5000 re-breaks the renderer, and no census of the altair row limit (alt.py:377, alt.py:386, alt.py:404) or pointer to `MaxRowsError`/`disable_max_rows` appears in the plan

findings.reason: one generalised control retires the label on both matplotlib stacks in a single pass, whereas a trace-only keyword leaves `ψ_norm` to need its own flag later and the plan's own argument ("extends that mechanism") is only half-honoured.
findings.text: §2 adds a trace-specific `label_time` keyword for one of the two `sharex` stacks that repeat an axis label, leaving the sibling unsuppressed: `radial_profile_figure_mpl` builds a `sharex=True` stack (figures.py:139) and calls `render_mpl(ax_i, rp)` per panel (figures.py:143), whose renderer `_render_radialprofile_mpl` sets `ax.set_xlabel("ψ_norm")` unconditionally on every panel (mpl.py:590), the same repeated-label defect the plan repairs at `_render_timeseries_mpl` (mpl.py:577) for `time_trace_figure_mpl` (figures.py:89, figures.py:95, figures.py:100); the census of the repeated-shared-axis-label type is therefore two live matplotlib stacks (time traces and radial profiles), and the altair stack repeats `Time [s]` too (alt.py:393, concatenated in imas_ink/server/mcp.py:300) — the plan acknowledges and declines the altair one but is silent on the radial-profile instance; the owner to extend is the shared axis-label control in the mpl renderers (mpl.py:549, mpl.py:583), generalised to a per-axis label flag, with `radial_profile_figure_mpl` sharing it

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v3 §2 generalises the keyword to label_x on both private renderers (_render_timeseries_mpl and _render_radialprofile_mpl), driven by both stacked builders, and tests both stacks

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v3 §1 states altair's default transformer refuses more than 5,000 rows (MaxRowsError), so a long series cannot be drawn in altair today, and sets trace_max_points to 4000, below that limit, so the envelope makes it renderable
